title: Taking over a job in Mexico and the audience there
summary: Goudie explains how he got to keep his room and took over a departing musician's place in Mexico; the audience was mixed nationalities with no colour prejudice.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: So they asked me, he says, when my job finished, you see, when my job finished, they asked me if I wanted to stay in my room. I said, sure, and that was luck, you know, and I didn't want to go back to the state, you know. That was really jammed up in my king. I said, I jump on it, I said, sure, because he says, you see, we can't have him, Charlie, and so far, because his wife had already sent him a ticket, you know, the money for him to come back to New Orleans, and he took that money and drank it up. And so he didn't go, because he didn't have the money, so she, Frank wrote to his wife, said, send him a ticket, don't send him the money. So she wired him a ticket, and he couldn't sell it, or he had to use it, or leave it. And so he went back. That's how I took his place, you see.
How was the reception for your type of music? Good.
Well, yes, the people liked it, and while we was waiting at the influence there was more or less Americans, Canadians, and German, French.
There wasn't any color bullshit at that time, was there?
